questions.question: What do the two swords worn by Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji represent?
options: Miri and Piri (temporal and spiritual authority)
questions.explanation: At his accession Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji wore two swords: Miri for temporal authority and Piri for spiritual authority.
questions.source: SGPC: Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji

questions.question: Which institution, facing Sri Harmandir Sahib, did Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji establish?
questions.explanation: Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji raised the Akal Takht opposite Sri Harmandir Sahib and conducted the community's temporal affairs from there.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia: Akal Takht
questions.note: Founding year not asked (1606 vs 1609 in sources).

questions.question: In which fort did Emperor Jahangir imprison Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji?
questions.explanation: Jahangir had Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji detained in the fort at Gwalior.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia: Gwalior
questions.note: Dates of imprisonment vary by source; not asked.

questions.question: According to Sikh tradition, how many imprisoned kings and princes were freed along with Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji from Gwalior?
questions.explanation: The Guru refused to leave alone; holding the 52 tassels of his cloak, 52 captive chiefs and princes walked out with him.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia: Gwalior

questions.question: What title did Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji earn after securing the release of fellow prisoners at Gwalior?
questions.explanation: He became known as Data Bandi Chhor, 'the Munificent Deliverer', for freeing the captives held with him.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia: Gwalior

questions.question: Which Sikh observance celebrates Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji's release from Gwalior and his return to Amritsar?
questions.explanation: Amritsar was lit up on his return, and Sikhs celebrate Bandi Chhor Divas at Diwali time.
questions.source: SGPC: Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji

questions.question: Who was the father of Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji?
questions.explanation: Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji was the only son of Guru Arjan Dev Ji and Mata Ganga Ji.
questions.source: SGPC: Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji

questions.question: Whom did Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji name as his successor, the seventh Guru?
options: His son, Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji
His grandson, Guru Har Rai Ji
questions.explanation: Before passing away, Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji named his grandson Har Rai, son of Baba Gurditta Ji, as the Seventh Nanak.
questions.source: SGPC: Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji

questions.question: At about what age did Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji become Guru?
questions.explanation: He succeeded Guru Arjan Dev Ji in 1606 at the age of eleven, after his father's martyrdom.
questions.source: SGPC: Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji

questions.question: Through his first hukamnama after raising the Akal Takht, what did Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji ask Sikhs to bring as offerings?
questions.explanation: His hukamnama to distant sangats asked Sikhs to include weapons and horses in their offerings from then on.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia: Akal Takht

questions.question: Where did Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji spend his last years and leave his body in 1644?
questions.explanation: From 1635 he lived at Kiratpur Sahib in the Shivalik foothills, and passed away there in 1644.
questions.source: SGPC: Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji

questions.question: Which son of Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji founded the town of Kiratpur Sahib on his father's instructions?
questions.explanation: Baba Gurditta Ji, the Guru's eldest son, founded Kiratpur in the Shivalik foothills under his father's instructions.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gurditta, Baba

questions.question: Which Sikh recovered the horses Dilbagh and Gulbagh, meant for Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji, from the Lahore governor's stables?
questions.explanation: Bhai Bidhi Chand, a commander in the Guru's army, recovered Dilbagh disguised as a hay-seller and Gulbagh disguised as an astrologer.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia: Bidhi Chand, Bhai

questions.question: Gurdwara Baba Atal in Amritsar, built in memory of Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji's son Baba Atal Rai, has how many storeys?
questions.explanation: The nine-storey octagonal tower recalls the nine years of Baba Atal Rai's short life.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia: Atal Rai, Baba

questions.question: Which Pathan commander, once close to Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji, turned against him and was killed in the battle of Kartarpur?
questions.explanation: Painda Khan, a childhood friend and commander in the Guru's army, deserted to the Mughals and was killed at Kartarpur in 1635.
questions.source: SGPC: Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji

questions.question: What was the name of Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji's only daughter?
questions.explanation: Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji had one daughter, Bibi Viro Ji, and five sons.
questions.source: SGPC: Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji

questions.question: Where was Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji born?
questions.explanation: Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji was born in 1595 at Guru ki Wadali in Amritsar district.
questions.source: SGPC: Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji

questions.question: Which small fort did Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji build at Amritsar?
questions.explanation: Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji built a wall around Amritsar and the small fort of Lohgarh on the town's western side.
questions.source: SGPC: Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji

questions.question: According to SGPC, the battle at Amritsar between Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji's Sikhs and Mughal troops began with a dispute over what?
questions.explanation: A quarrel over a royal hawk led Mukhlis Khan to attack the Sikhs at Amritsar; the Sikhs repulsed the attack and Mukhlis Khan was killed.
questions.source: SGPC: Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji
questions.note: Year of the Amritsar battle differs (1629 vs 1634) by source; not asked.

questions.question: Which sarovar did Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji have built near Mehraj to mark victory in the battle of the Lakhi Jungle?
questions.explanation: After the Sikh victory near Mehraj and Lahira, the Guru built the Gurusar tank to mark the occasion.
questions.source: SGPC: Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji
